Jaminin

Overview

Jaminin is a necromancer whose theoretical learning proves inadequate in practice. His experiment unleashes undead and lands him in the baron’s custody. Under questioning he provides a way to stop the disaster using a potion at the cemetery and an incantation, revealing the gap between his scholarly ambitions and his competence. [1, 2, 3]

Jaminin’s experiment and the undead

The trail of the local undead leads to Jaminin on Death Island. Brought before the baron, he bargains for his life with the promise of useful knowledge. Kir and Kel obtain a potion from a tomb, but need to know how to apply it across the affected area. Jaminin first entertains a human sacrifice; Kel rejects it, and he supplies a less destructive method involving cemetery soil and an incantation. The potion puts the dead to rest. His later exchanges preserve the distinction between theoretical learning and practical competence: he possesses information, but his own experiment caused the disaster. Their success also changes the baron’s view of Kel. He admits that her achievements have repeatedly disproved his claim that war is no business for women. [4, 1, 2, 5, 3, 6, 7]
